title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let \hat\pi_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,\infty}, i.e. free profinite on two generators. Let \mathfrak S_3 act on it through the extended group \hat\pi_{0,3}\rtimes\mathfrak S_3. This is the orbifold group of M_{0,3} modulo \mathfrak S_3, a 'cote' structure. The generators are the involution \sigma_\infty (swapping 0 and 1) and the order-3 element \rho (cyclically permuting 0, 1, \infty). Put \varepsilon_0=\sigma_\infty\rho; its square is the inertia generator l_0, and L_0=\overline{\langle l_0\rangle} is the inertia (loop) subgroup at 0.

The groups. M^{!\sim}_{0,3} is the group of automorphisms of \hat\pi_{0,3} commuting exteriorly with \mathfrak S_3. M^{!\sim}_{0,3}[0] is its subgroup normalising L_0.

What the page does. Grothendieck 'recapitulates' and proposes to study the big group through this subgroup. He writes
- u(\sigma_\infty)=\eta\sigma_\infty and u(\rho)=\xi\rho, with \eta,\xi\in\hat\pi_{0,3} (128)-(129). These express exterior commutation with \mathfrak S_3.
- Normalisation of L_0 is encoded as u(\varepsilon_0)=\varepsilon_0^{\mu}, equivalently u(l_0)=l_0^{\mu}, with \mu\in\hat{\mathbb Z}^* (130).

Computation.
1. u(\varepsilon_0)=\eta\sigma_\infty\xi\rho=\eta\,\sigma_\infty(\xi)\,\varepsilon_0, where \sigma_\infty(\cdot) denotes conjugation.
2. Hence \eta\sigma_\infty(\xi)=\varepsilon_0^{\mu-1}. Write \mu-1=2\nu; this is possible since units of \hat{\mathbb Z} have unit 2-adic component. Then \eta\sigma_\infty(\xi)=l_0^{\nu}.
3. Applying \sigma_\infty, which sends l_0 to l_1, gives \sigma_\infty(\eta)\xi=l_1^{\nu}.
4. The relations (\eta\sigma_\infty)^2=1 and (\xi\rho)^3=1, which say the images of the generators keep their orders, rewrite as
   - \eta\,\sigma_\infty(\eta)=1,
   - \xi\,\rho(\xi)\,\rho^2(\xi)=1 (133).
5. Hence \sigma_\infty(\eta)=\eta^{-1}, and the loop relation becomes \xi=\eta\, l_1^{\nu} (134).

The next page states the theorem. Elements of M^{!\sim}_{0,3}[0] correspond bijectively to pairs (\xi,\eta) satisfying (133)-(134), plus a 'liminary' surjectivity condition. The quotient by L_0 recovers N^{!\sim}_{0,3}.

Modern reading. With \eta=f(x,y) and \lambda=\mu=2\nu+1 (so \nu=m in Drinfeld's notation):
- \eta\sigma_\infty(\eta)=1 is the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1.
- \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1 with \xi=\eta l_1^{\nu} is the 3-cycle (hexagon) relation f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m=1.

So the page derives, in 1981, the two defining relations of Drinfeld's \widehat{GT} (1990), without the pentagon. The group in question is the profinite group of pairs (\lambda,f) satisfying (I) and (II). It is presented as the automorphism group of \hat\pi_{0,3} commuting with \mathfrak S_3 and normalising inertia. This is the standard M_{0,4}-level ('GT_0'-type) description.
errors: (130) asserts that normalising L_0 is equivalent to u(\varepsilon_0)=\varepsilon_0^{\mu}. This needs a small argument: the square roots of l_0^{\mu} in the relevant coset are unique, since the centraliser of l_0 in the extended group is generated by \varepsilon_0. The marginal note (130bis) suggests Grothendieck was checking this equivalence; the gap is minor.
The equation number (131) is used twice: once for the computation of u(\varepsilon_0), once for \sigma_\infty(\eta)\xi=l_1^{\nu}. This is cosmetic.

The identity \sigma_\infty(l_0)=l_1 is used exactly, not merely up to conjugacy. This depends on the choice of base/tangential point compatible with \sigma_\infty; it is implicit but fine with the standard normalisation.

ideas.what: Describing automorphisms of \hat\pi_{0,3} that commute exteriorly with \mathfrak S_3 and normalise inertia by pairs (\eta,\xi) with u(\sigma_\infty)=\eta\sigma_\infty and u(\rho)=\xi\rho.
ideas.where_published: Theme of La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) and Esquisse d'un programme (1984), which mentions \mathfrak S_3-compatible automorphisms; the explicit formulas are probably not published

ideas.what: The relations \eta\sigma_\infty(\eta)=1 and \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1 with \xi=\eta l_1^{\nu} and \mu=2\nu+1\in\hat{\mathbb Z}^*.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 (On quasitriangular quasi-Hopf algebras and Gal(\bar Q/Q)); Ihara
ideas.where_published: Possibly reflected in Schneps' account of the Longue Marche in Geometric Galois Actions I (1997); unsure whether this exact derivation is reproduced

ideas.what: Writing \mu-1=2\nu, i.e. the exponent \lambda of a \widehat{GT}-element is odd and the hexagon exponent is m=(\lambda-1)/2.

missed.claim: In 1981, before Drinfeld (1990), Grothendieck derives in this archival continuation of the Longue Marche the two-cycle and three-cycle relations defining \widehat{GT} (without the pentagon). He also characterises the solutions as automorphisms commuting exteriorly with \mathfrak S_3 and normalising L_0. The general fact that the Longue Marche anticipates parts of GT is known through Schneps, so the novelty is the explicit derivation in this part of the archive (140-3).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority documentation for the GT relations. It also gives a clean group-theoretic characterisation in terms of the orbifold \hat\pi_{0,3}\rtimes\mathfrak S_3 and normalisation of inertia, a viewpoint close to recent work on the 'GT-hat equals Out of braid/orbifold groups' type.

missed.claim: On the next page Grothendieck notes that the invertibility condition 2\nu+1\in\hat{\mathbb Z}^* follows from (133)-(134). He also raises whether the 'liminary' surjectivity condition is implied by the relations. Whether the relations alone force bijectivity is a question of current interest in the GT literature.
missed.quote: la condition \nu-liminaire 2\nu+1\in\hat{\mathbb Z}^* (qui est impliquée par la condition liminaire, et peut-être l'impliquera...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In the GT literature the invertibility of (\lambda,f) is usually imposed separately. A proof that the relations imply it would simplify the definition of \widehat{GT}.

deep.surprise_reason: The page derives Drinfeld's 2-cycle and hexagon relations nearly a decade before Drinfeld. That Grothendieck's Longue Marche anticipated GT-type relations is partly known through Schneps' commentaries, so this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a genuine surprise.
transcription_corrections: 'les automorphismes à la cote de \hat\pi_{0,3}' is likely 'les automorphismes ext.^s de \hat\pi_{0,3}' or similar; the reading is uncertain.
The second equation labelled (131), \sigma_\infty(\eta)\xi=l_1^\nu, is marked '(*31)' in the manuscript.
The marginal note reads roughly: '(130) équivaut à u normalise L_0 ... (130bis) u(\xi_1)=int(\rho)(\xi_1^\mu)..., u(\varepsilon_0)=int(...)(\varepsilon_0^\mu)'. It is partly illegible.
The page header '207' is Grothendieck's own pagination.
